clue.text: It's calamitous when soldiers fall into the river

indicators.note: the soldiers drop inside the river's name, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops tumbling into a river would be a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Something calamitous brings disaster, often causing death, as a deadly outcome does.

clue.text: First and last letters to Rose out in Portuguese islands

parts.note: A and Z open and close the alphabet

indicators.note: out here means disordered, so the letters of the word Rose are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sends letters to a woman called Rose, who is away in the Atlantic islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First and last letters' means those of the alphabet, not of any clue word; 'out' turns ROSE into ORES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Azores are an Atlantic archipelago belonging to Portugal.

clue.text: It's no advantage to retire

explanation.surface: Retreating brings no benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawback is a disadvantage; to draw back is to withdraw or retreat.

clue.text: Visit park and refuse to leave

parts.note: to stay with someone is to visit them
to park something is to put it down somewhere

explanation.surface: A visitor to a park won't go home.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay put is to remain where one is, declining to move.

clue.text: Ground facility to aid flier in difficulties

indicators.note: the words aid flier are in trouble, so their letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A base on land helps a pilot who is in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: An airfield is a ground installation where aircraft take off and land.

clue.text: Make effective tool

explanation.surface: Put a useful instrument to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To implement a plan is to carry it out; an implement is an instrument or utensil.

clue.text: Laze or tan in resort known for winter and summer sun

definitions.text: known for winter and summer sun

indicators.note: read as re-sort, sorted again, so the letters of Laze or tan are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Lounging or drinking from a can at a holiday spot that is sunny all year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like part of the definition, but is the anagram signal (re-sort); the definition is the descriptive tail, naming a Canary Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanzarote, one of the Canary Islands, is a holiday island with sunshine all year round.

clue.text: Companies supply wood and paper for publication

parts.note: fir is a kind of timber tree
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a text submitted for printing

explanation.surface: Businesses provide timber and paper to the printing trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Firms are business concerns, synonyms for companies.

clue.text: First sign of rust in rotten nail

indicators.note: the opening letter goes inside the word for rotten

parts.note: rotten food is bad

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word rust is taken

explanation.surface: Rust showing on a decayed nail.
explanation.definitionFit: A brad is a thin, small-headed wire nail.

clue.text: Larry won somehow, but not by a lot

indicators.note: somehow suggests the words Larry won are worked over in some fashion, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Larry triumphed in some way, but only just.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning narrowly means by a small margin.

clue.text: A lot may be held in it

definitions.text: A lot may be held in it

parts.words: A lot may be held in it
parts.note: a lot reads as a large amount, but here it is a numbered ticket or prize held in a draw

explanation.surface: Something capacious enough to hold a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A raffle is a lottery-style draw in which tickets, or lots, are drawn for prizes.

clue.text: Every atlas, I assume, will include it

definitions.text: Every atlas, I assume, will include it

indicators.note: the words atlas, I assume contain the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: Surely any atlas will have this continent in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and the letters sit across 'atlAS I Assume'.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest continent, which any world atlas maps.

clue.text: Unforeseen turn made awkwardly

indicators.note: awkwardly made suggests the letters of turn made are clumsily rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone made an unexpected turn clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: Undreamt-of things were never imagined, so they were not anticipated.

clue.text: It involves places and composition

indicators.note: composition means putting together, so the letters of places and are composed anew

explanation.surface: A painted scene is built from places arranged into a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a painting of scenery is a composition of places.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a picture of countryside scenery, an artistic arrangement of places.

clue.text: Coming down on Shrove Tuesday?

parts.note: a flipped batter dish descending to the pan on the day it is traditionally eaten

explanation.surface: Something falling on the day before Lent.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrove Tuesday is the British name for the day before Lent, when batter dishes are traditionally made and tossed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pancake landing is an emergency touchdown where an aircraft drops flat onto its belly.

clue.text: Clear course of action after study

indicators.note: the battle's name comes after the word for study

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study
the Somme was a major First World War battle, a military action

explanation.surface: A plain path of conduct follows careful study.
explanation.definitionFit: Consomme is a clear soup served as a course of a meal.

clue.text: See 15
Frantic chase for one's principal opponents

indicators.note: frantic suggests wild disorder, so the letters of chase for are scrambled

explanation.surface: A wild pursuit of one's chief enemies.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch here means chief, so these are a person's leading enemies.

clue.text: Enthusiasts may wax it

parts.note: wax looks like polishing, but here it is the old verb meaning to grow or become, in a fixed phrase for speaking effusively

explanation.surface: Keen hobbyists polishing something.
explanation.definitionFit: To wax lyrical is to speak about something with great enthusiasm.

clue.text: Be able to say who's who I find, yet all confused

definitions.text: Be able to say who's who

indicators.note: the words I find, yet are muddled together, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone discovers they are still mixed up about who people are.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify people is to recognise them and name them correctly.

clue.text: One to get upset over a trifle

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in a down answer upset means turned upside down, so the word to is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone becomes distressed about a small matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get upset' turns TO into OT; 'over' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota, the smallest Greek letter, means a tiny amount, a mere jot.

clue.text: Laws the expert may break

explanation.surface: A specialist might break the law.
explanation.definitionFit: A code is both a set of statutes and a secret cipher that codebreakers solve.

clue.text: Describing Hamlet and his difficulty

parts.note: Shakespeare's prince came from Denmark, and his difficulty is that he is a Dane

explanation.surface: An account of Shakespeare's prince and his indecision.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet was Prince of Denmark, so he is of that nation.

clue.text: Expert to give way under pressure

explanation.surface: A specialist cracks under stress.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack shot is an expert one; to crack is to break down when strained.

clue.text: Confront with a small account charge

parts.note: a/c is the short form of account
a charge is a cost or fee

explanation.surface: Challenging someone over a minor fee on a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and address them boldly.

clue.text: Uniformed footmen

parts.note: footmen suggests liveried servants, but here means soldiers who fight on foot

explanation.surface: Household servants in livery.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantry are foot soldiers, who wear military uniform.

clue.text: MP and Sue frolic in the foam

indicators.note: frolic suggests playful capering, so the letters of MP and Sue are tumbled about

explanation.surface: A politician and a woman called Sue play in the surf.
explanation.definitionFit: Spume is froth or foam on waves.

clue.text: Pack horse used around States!

indicators.note: the horse word is placed around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a hack is a riding horse
to aver is to state firmly, so avers means states

explanation.surface: A packhorse used across the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' looks like the USA but is the verb meaning declares.
explanation.definitionFit: A haversack is a bag or knapsack carried on the back.
